results.content:
Hey Product Hunt!  
  
I work with app developers all day, and I wanted a game about what that job actually feels like. So Ship It is an idle tycoon where you start with one developer in a tiny office, ship updates, and slowly build a studio. Along the way, things go wrong the way they do in real life: servers go down on a Friday, an SDK gets sunset, and App Review rejects your build when the tech debt gets out of hand  
  
Version 2.0 just went live. It adds an App Review mechanic, incidents, a Hall of Fame that carries across studio sales, and a Game Center leaderboard for your lifetime fortune  
  
There are also 68 collectible advisers. Some of them might look a little familiar if you spend time on tech Twitter :) [...] Subscribe

results.content:
#### vs Alternatives

 Startup Company (Steam): A fantastic, deeply modular business sandbox game where you build out physical office layouts and manage server infrastructure. However, it requires a financial commitment, a local download, and can sometimes feel more like a middle-management logistics simulator than a fast-paced founder experience.
 Game Dev Tycoon: The classic benchmark for developer sims, but its mechanics are firmly rooted in traditional retail game launches rather than modern, cloud-based continuous deployment and subscription metrics.
 Idle Startup Tycoon: A fun browser-based clicker on platforms like Poki. While highly accessible, it relies on hyper-casual, hands-off idle progression rather than strategic decision-making and actual SaaS math. [...] Report

results.title: AgentSky: One API, Every Agent - Openrouter for Agents | Product Hunt
results.content:
A health check tells you the process is alive. It does not tell you the work moved. Those two come apart exactly in long horizon agents, which is the case you are built for. An agent stuck on the same step for six hours is healthy. An agent waiting on a webhook that will never fire is healthy. An agent that finished twenty minutes ago is healthy. All three pass the check, and all three are indistinguishable from idle.

I have had precisely this. Scheduled work stopped and every check kept answering correctly, because the machine was up, the job was scheduled, and nothing was in an error state, because nothing had errored. What had actually stopped was not a unit anything was watching. [...] So the signal I would put next to the health check is last progress rather than last heartbeat. Something the agent advances only when it completes a unit of work, plus a declared expectation of how often that should happen. That is what stops healthy and stuck being the same state.

On the second, agreed it cannot be solved in general, but I would cut it differently than by product. It is not really a matter of opinion, it is reads versus side effects. Best effort on a read is fine, you fetch again and nobody notices. Best effort on a send means a customer gets the same WhatsApp message twice, and no amount of application level opinion prevents that. [...] It's reachable wherever your users already are — WhatsApp, iMessage, Telegram, Slack, web, CLI, or our developer API's. Same protocol, same memory, every harness, every channel.

Already battle-tested in production, AgentSky powers tycoon.us, where it has handled over 10K+ agent sessions.

Parking an agent is free — you only pay when it's actively working.

Would love your feedback, especially on which runtimes and channels you'd want next!

Dale Mooney

Suspend and resume is the interesting part, and I think it has a blind spot worth designing for now rather than later.
